Given no extensions, when `[a](https://example.com)` is converted, then the result is `

a

`.

Given no extensions, when `` is converted, then the result is `

https://example.com

`.

Given extension `external_links`, when `[a](https://example.com)` is converted, then the result is `

a

a

Given extension `external_links`, when `[a][1]` with the definition `[1]: https://example.com` is converted, then the `<a>` element in the result contains `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

Given extension `external_links`, when `` is converted, then the result is `

https://example.com

a

`.

a

Given extension `external_links`, when `![a](https://example.com/i.png)` is converted, then the result is `

`.

questions.options: (a) existing value is kept (b) extension value overwrites (c) `rel` merged, `target` kept (d) Other

questions.question: Are `HTTP://example.com` and `//example.com` external?
questions.options: (a) neither is external, exact lowercase prefix only (b) uppercase schemes are external, `//` is not (c) both are external (d) Other

` are all stated, so a unit test can assert on the return value and on the absence of an exception.
The constructor call with the extension is fully specified, and the outcome (no exception raised) is observable.
With no extensions, the input and the exact expected HTML string are given, so the output can be compared directly.
The autolink input and the exact expected HTML string are stated, so the output can be compared directly.

The autolink input with the extension and the exact expected HTML string are stated.
A relative link input and the exact expected HTML with no target or rel attributes are given.
A fragment link input and the exact expected HTML with no target or rel attributes are given.
The mailto input is given and the outcome is a clear observable check that neither `target=` nor `rel=` appears.
The image input and the exact expected `` HTML are stated.
The nested image-in-link input is given, and the test can parse the result and check attribute presence on the `` and `` elements; the relative link target follows from AC-FR-005.
